newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba slams Spain's foreign minister over remarks.
newsitem.headline: Cuba slams Spain's foreign minister over remarks.

text.p: Cuba attacked Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes on Thursday over remarks he made about Cuba after a Spanish tourist was not permitted to leave the island following his involvement in a traffic accident.
Cuban Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina told a news conference that Matutes was "a liar, a blackmailer and an interferer."
Robaina said Matutes' version of events concerning tourist Jesus Martin was full of errors and the Spanish minister's comments had been "arrogant, interfering and above all false."

His angry reaction followed remarks on Wednesday by Matutes, who said Spain would consider issuing a travel advisory recommending that its citizens not travel to Cuba if the Martin case was not resolved satisfactorily.

Martin has been prevented from leaving for home since the accident, which Robaina said occurred on March 1 and not last month as Matutes stated. Robaina said this was normal and added that Martin had never been detained, apart from the time needed to take his statement following the accident.

The argument over the tourist is the latest upset in relations between Spain and Cuba. Ties have been tense since Spain's conservative government under Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar took office last May, promising a tougher stance on Cuba than its Socialist predecessor.
